description: AstroSimX is a team passionate about space exploration, technology, AI, and software development. We are building ORBITX, an interactive Space Mission Design Simulator. Our interests include web development, 3D simulations, UI/UX, and problem-solving. We welcome passionate team players who want to innovate and learn together. Looking for members skilled in React, JavaScript, 3D design, astronomy, physics, UI/UX, and presentation.
summary:
ORBITX is an interactive space mission design and simulation game developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It allows players to experience the challenges of spacecraft engineering by designing spacecraft, selecting scientific instruments, managing resources, and operating missions to the Moon, Mars, and near-Earth asteroids.

Players configure six spacecraft subsystems and evaluate mass, budget, propulsion, power, battery reserves, and communication performance using deterministic, simplified engineering models. They can launch missions, monitor real-time telemetry, respond to emergencies, and explore a procedural 3D space environment.

ORBITX also integrates NASA and JPL public data, including asteroid observations, solar activity, astronomical reference data, and Earth imagery. An AI Mission Advisor provides educational guidance while keeping numerical simulation results under the control of the deterministic game engine.

The project makes space exploration and mission engineering more accessible by turning complex concepts into an interactive educational experience.
details:
ORBITX is a browser-based educational space mission design and simulation game that transforms real-world aerospace engineering concepts into interactive gameplay.

How it works: Players begin by selecting one of three mission scenarios: Lunar Reconnaissance, Mars Exploration, or Asteroid Observation. They then design a spacecraft using six subsystems: structure, power generation, energy storage, propulsion, telecommunications, and scientific payload.

The engineering engine calculates spacecraft mass, budget, Delta-V, solar power, battery reserves, and communication link margins using documented simplified mathematical models. Players must satisfy mission constraints before locking their spacecraft and launching a mission.

During flight, players progress through seven mission stages, monitor telemetry, manage resources, and respond to deterministic emergency scenarios. A procedural Three.js environment provides interactive planetary visualization, orbital trajectories, and spacecraft tracking.

NASA data integration: ORBITX connects to NASA NeoWs, DONKI, NASA APOD, JPL Horizons, and NASA GIBS through server-side API routes. Retrieved data is distinguished from simulated gameplay values.

Technology: React, TypeScript, Vite, Three.js, React Three Fiber, Drei, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, Node.js, Express, and Google Gemini API.

Artificial Intelligence: The AI Mission Advisor provides educational explanations, risk analysis, and context-aware recommendations. A deterministic offline knowledge base ensures continued availability. AI does not control or modify engineering calculations.

Impact: ORBITX makes aerospace engineering more accessible to students and space enthusiasts through experimentation, decision-making, scientific learning, and interactive simulation. It demonstrates how gaming and real space science resources can work together to support STEM education.

The simulator uses simplified educational models and is not intended for real spacecraft flight planning.
